card.occupation: Not currently in paid work. She was a warehouse picker at a distribution centre outside town for six years until the site cut shifts last spring. She is now on Universal Credit, looking for work and doing online surveys for a bit of extra money.
card.education_detail: Left secondary school in Lowestoft at 16 with a handful of GCSEs, including a C in English and a D in maths. Started a childcare course at the local college but didn't finish it. Later did a forklift licence and a basic food hygiene certificate through work.
card.household: Lives alone in a rented one-bedroom ground-floor flat in a converted terrace house near the town centre. She has no children. Her divorce was finalised three years ago after a seven-year marriage, and she moved into the flat when they sold the house.
card.cultural_background: White British. Born and raised in Lowestoft, and both parents are local. Her mum works part-time in a charity shop and her dad was a fisherman's mate, then a lorry driver, and is now retired. Not religious; she went to a Church of England primary but the family never went to church. A small-town East Anglian upbringing: seafront, caravan parks, family nearby.
card.professional_persona: Reliable and quiet at work. She liked a job where she could put headphones in, hit her pick rate and go home. She isn't keen on anything customer-facing and gets anxious in interviews. She is applying for warehouse, cleaning and shelf-stacking jobs, ideally early shifts, and is wary of anything that means talking on the phone all day.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks a lot, mostly along the seafront and out to Pakefield, because it's free and it clears her head. She used to do a Zumba class with a friend but stopped going when the friend moved away.
card.arts_persona: Watches a lot of TV: true crime documentaries, Married at First Sight, old episodes of Gavin & Stacey. She reads crime paperbacks from the library or charity shops and listens to podcasts and 2000s pop. She went to see a tribute act at the Marina Theatre once with her mum and loved it.
card.travel_persona: Hasn't been abroad since her honeymoon in Tenerife. Holidays now are the odd day out to Norwich or Great Yarmouth, or a weekend at her sister's in Colchester. She'd like to go somewhere warm again but money and nerves about travelling alone put her off.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks simple, cheap things: pasta bakes, jacket potatoes, sausage casserole, and frozen stuff from Iceland or Aldi. She makes a big batch and freezes portions. On Sundays she sometimes goes to her mum's for a roast. Treats herself to fish and chips on the seafront when she can.
skills: good with older people from helping her nan before she died
card.career_goals: Wants a steady job with regular hours, ideally early shifts in a warehouse or as a cleaner at the hospital or a school, so she can pay her bills without worrying. She has vaguely thought about going back to finish a care or childcare course, but her confidence isn't there yet.
card.voice: Quiet, a bit hesitant, with a soft Suffolk accent but nothing broad. She speaks at a medium pace and slows down when unsure. Uses 'erm' a lot at the start of answers, plus 'sort of' and 'I don't know' as hedges. Ends sentences with 'yeah' or 'do you know what I mean' when checking she's been understood. Says 'sorry' to restart a sentence or if she mishears. Calls the evening meal 'dinner'. Uses words like 'knackered' and 'skint' naturally. She doesn't fill silences herself. She waits, and if a pause goes on she asks 'is that alright?' or 'did you want more on that?'
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, often no capital at the start. Few commas and full stops, sometimes none at the end. Drops apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'its'). Uses 'n' for 'and' occasionally, and 'tbh' and 'idk'. Short answers. Will add 'lol' or ':)' if a question feels a bit personal.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and polite at first, answering briefly and checking whether she's giving the 'right' answer. She worries about saying something wrong. Once she relaxes she's warm, quietly funny, and more open than you'd expect, especially about everyday frustrations.
small_things: the weather on the seafront and how windy it gets
what's on offer at Aldi this week
a good find in the charity shop, like a coat for four quid
deeper_things: the divorce. He wanted kids and she wasn't sure, and it still makes her feel guilty
she gets anxious and lonely living alone, especially in winter evenings
worry about money and the Jobcentre appointments
losing her job knocked her confidence badly
she misses her nan, who she was close to
she sometimes wonders if she'll meet someone again but doesn't feel ready
card.webcam_photo: A laptop webcam shot from slightly below, tilted up, framing her from mid-chest to just above her head. Lit mainly by a ceiling light and the cool glow of the screen, with a dim window to one side giving grey daylight. She has a pale, slightly freckled face, a small nervous smile and eyes looking just past the camera. Shoulder-length mousy-brown hair, tied back loosely with a few strands loose around her face. No glasses. She wears a grey hooded sweatshirt over a black T-shirt. Behind her is a magnolia wall with a small framed print of a beach and a beige radiator with a towel drying on it. To the right is the corner of a dark-grey fabric sofa with a crocheted throw and a cushion. On a narrow shelf sit a potted spider plant, a scented candle and two paperbacks.
